★ Sheriff's Race

02 / 05
The Race at a Glance

Two veterans, one open seat

Doug Seifert

Front-runner
  • 20-year BCSO veteran; former lieutenant & town councilman
  • Endorsed by retiring Sheriff P.J. Tanner ("the future of this office")
  • Won county GOP straw poll 51%–31% (May 17)
  • Message: continuity — build on existing operations, recruit & retain

JoJo Woodward

Challenger
  • 35+ years in law enforcement; former BCSO captain
  • Third bid for sheriff (lost to Tanner in 2018 & 2022)
  • Tanner publicly opposes him — "a character issue you can't overcome"
  • Message: change — cut command staff, raise deputy pay to $64K
03 / 05
Who's Running the Better Campaign

Seifert owns the institutional lane

Both run real operations, but they're fighting different battles. Seifert built a broad, multi-message machine. Woodward is running a near-pure endorsement-defense play to blunt Tanner's attack.

Seifert — Range & reach

  • Crown-jewel endorsement: the sitting 28-year sheriff
  • Diversified content: issues, social proof, momentum, emotional storytelling
  • Backed by money — boosted/paid reels driving big numbers
  • Reads as the consensus, establishment-and-base candidate

Woodward — Credibility chase

  • Nearly every post is another endorsement announcement
  • Backers (Newton, Herbkersman, Sulka, a Jasper sheriff) are lower-wattage & cluster in his Bluffton base
  • Best original asset: "The Hollis Standard" child-safety policy
  • Strategy is fundamentally defensive — proving he belongs

The Call · June 9 GOP Primary

Prediction

Doug Seifert
57%
Projected winner
JoJo Woodward
43%
Challenger

Every directional signal points the same way: sheriff's endorsement, a 20-point straw-poll lead, apparent rank-and-file deputy support, and a commanding social reach advantage. The margin is pulled in from the straw poll's 20 points because rally crowds over-represent the engaged base, while Woodward's two prior runs give him real name recognition and a built-in protest vote.

Honest caveat: there is no scientific poll here. This is an inference from organization and momentum, not a measurement — and primary turnout in a low-profile June race skews older and may never see any of this content.

Sources: Island Packet / Beaufort Gazette, WTOC, WSAV, WJCL, The Island News, Beaufort County GOP straw poll (5/17/26), and campaign Facebook pages. Analysis prepared June 4, 2026 — five days before the primary. Predictive, not authoritative.
